belay.8: Belay at the bolts out to the left, so the rope does not pinch behind the big wedged block.

belay.2: A small tree at the foot of the obvious left-facing corner, reached by stepping off the big tree ledge.
belay.3: A comfortable ledge with a tree at the top of the left-facing corner.
belay.4: A stance beneath the roof, near a dead-end chimney that the route does not climb.
belay.6: An alcove reached above the offwidth, after passing the two bolts.

belay.1: Stop at the top of the stair-stepped gully and build the anchor in a crack there.
belay.2: The belay is on a rock shelf holding a couple of small pools, with solid cracks for anchor gear.
belay.4-8: Head for the stubby tree on the upper right of the face, then belay at the next patch of small trees.

belay.3: The bolted anchor sits a few metres above the two bolts, up knobs and a finger crack.
belay.4: The anchor sits on a small ledge at the top of the pitch.
belay.7: Belay on the slab directly beneath the prominent roof system.
belay.8: Belay from a stance on the ridge.
